title: Combination and Decomposition Reactions Practice
description: Practice recognizing the patterns A + B -> AB and AB -> A + B.

questions.question: Which general pattern represents a combination reaction?
questions.explanation: A combination reaction forms one product from two or more reactants, so the pattern is A + B -> AB.

questions.question: Classify the reaction: 2Mg + O2 -> 2MgO.
questions.explanation: Two reactant substances, Mg and O2, form one product substance, MgO. That matches combination.

questions.question: A decomposition reaction starts with one reactant and forms two or more products.
questions.explanation: Decomposition follows the pattern AB -> A + B, where one substance breaks into simpler substances.

questions.question: Classify the reaction: 2H2O -> 2H2 + O2.
questions.explanation: One reactant substance, H2O, forms two product substances, H2 and O2. That is decomposition.

questions.question: Fill in the reaction type: A + B -> AB is a __________ reaction.
questions.explanation: Combination reactions are also called synthesis reactions because substances join to build one product.

questions.question: Which clue best identifies a decomposition reaction?
options: Many products join into one reactant
One reactant forms two or more products
questions.explanation: The main pattern clue for decomposition is one reactant breaking into two or more products.

questions.question: Coefficients alone determine whether a reaction is combination or decomposition.
questions.explanation: Coefficients help balance the equation. Reaction type is identified by the pattern of different reactant and product substances.

questions.question: In one or two sentences, explain why CaO + CO2 -> CaCO3 is a combination reaction.
questions.correctAnswer: It is a combination reaction because two reactant substances, CaO and CO2, join to form one product substance, CaCO3.
questions.explanation: The equation matches A + B -> AB: multiple reactants make a single product.
